brief: A service corridor inside a spruce-taiga hillside base. It connects the storage wing to the operator's room of a redstone part-picking machine; a live redstone signal line runs along the floor in a channel against the far wall.

score.notes: A clean, regular colonnade read head-on. Proportion is the build's strength: the bay rhythm is even and deliberate, and there is a legible base (stone plinth) → middle (column screen with recessed bays) → crown (timber entablature with a modest overhanging cornice). Nothing feels arbitrary, so it earns Strong here, though the massing stays low and horizontal with no central emphasis or climax. Color is disciplined but unremarkable — a dark stone/charcoal base, spruce-brown entablature, and dark column shafts form a coherent earthy scheme, with the lantern points as the only accent; pleasant and restrained rather than a scheme with real identity, and the overall darkness reads a touch muddy. Detail is the weak point relative to the brief: the recessed bays, lanterns, and stone plinth texture give some articulation and a sense of depth, but the column faces, entablature, and base are largely flat fields with shallow relief and little ornament — competent, not rich. Fidelity: it is clearly a repeating columned structure and recognizable as a classical portico/stoa, but it does not project grand-temple presence — no dominant entrance, no pediment or vertical accent, no landmark gesture; it reads as a long low arcade rather than an iconic temple. Holistically a tidy, well-ordered colonnade that is competent throughout — it would benefit most from a central focus and deeper, more varied relief to climb toward strong.

scoreRound0.notes: Read as a longitudinal corridor section against the brief, not as a temple facade (the fidelity anchor's temple framing doesn't match this hallway brief; judged as the decorated corridor it was meant to be). PROPORTION is the strength: a clean, regular bay rhythm set by evenly-spaced columns, with a legible base (floor band) → middle (lit alcove register) → crown (cornice line under a dark ceiling slab). Deliberate and coherent; held back from exceptional only because the bays are uniform rather than hierarchically composed (no accent bay, portal, or terminus). COLOR is disciplined and harmonious — dominant deepslate grey, supporting warm spruce/brown, and warm lantern glow as a consistent accent; the scheme suits a hillside service corridor well. DETAIL is where it stays competent: the articulation (recessed alcoves, projecting posts, lanterns, furnace/prop clutter that says who uses the space) is genuinely purposeful but confined almost entirely to the mid-band. The ceiling reads as a flat deepslate field and the floor is a plain band — large undecorated surfaces, and the named redstone signal channel against the far wall doesn't register at this scale. Treat/articulate the ceiling and floor and the whole thing lifts. FIDELITY is strong as the intended subject: it convincingly reads as a real, walkable, atmospherically lit corridor cut in section, with props establishing use. Easy improvements (flat ceiling/floor, single-register detail, uniform bays) are nameable, so it lands Strong, not exceptional.
